## Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly
22 September 2026 [UN Affairs](/en/news/topic/un-affairs)

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the General Assembly on Tuesday that the UN needs to become a “temple of peace” once again, as it confronts one of the most critical periods in its 80-year history.
Opening this year’s General Debate, the President – known to all as Lula – expressed his indignation at the widespread attacks taking place on multilateralism worldwide.
According to the Brazilian leader, more effective diplomacy is the only way for collective challenges to be successfully addressed.
He said the organization's credibility has been weakened due to paralysis of the [Security Council](https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/), the use of veto powers and growing geopolitical tensions.

“We are all held hostage by the inaction of the Security Council” he said, stressing that Brazil has spoken out against the use of veto power by permanent members in the chamber since the first general assembly meeting in 1946.
### **World of conflict**
The Brazilian leader recalled that the previous year had seen the highest number of armed conflicts registered since the Second World War.
He called for regional conflicts to be contained before they escalate into “tragedies of global proportions”.

Turning to the conflict in the Middle East, Lula said that “generations of Palestinians” will now carry “the pain and trauma left by the genocide of women and children,” criticising the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank – all making a two-State solution increasingly difficult to achieve.
Lula also addressed the war between Russia and Ukraine, saying the conflict had continued to claim lives and that there would be “no winners on the battlefield”.
### **Brazil’s path**

He also highlighted key policies at home, noting that Brazil has once again made inroads against hunger and adopted a new law to combat corruption and organised crime – which has led to a record level of seizures of drugs, assets and illicit funds.
“The fight against corruption shall remain relentless," Lula said. "No matter who it hurts. No one is above the law.”
### **Trusting science**
On climate change, President Lula said that, in an era of disinformation, those who reject scientific evidence are denying reality.
He said economic development should always go hand in hand with environmental protection.
The president also called for greater regulation of large technology companies and artificial intelligence (AI), warning against a technological race without ethical safeguards.
In his closing remarks, Lula highlighted the UN's historic role in decolonisation, human rights, sustainable development and the protection of migrants and refugees.
He called on Member States to find the political will to once again make the UN a “temple of peace”

## Index description

The Selic rate is the average interest rate charged on the daily interbank loans—with a maturity of one day (overnight) backed by federal government securities—registered in the Special System of Clearance and Custody (Selic). Specifically, the BCB’s Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) sets the target for the Selic rate every 45 days in a two-day meeting. Accordingly, open market operations are carried out in order to keep the daily effective Selic rate close to the target. In 1999 the Bank adopted inflation-targeting regime.

## Data sources
All data collected automatically from public databases of the **Central Bank of Brazil**, with no manual intervention:

-   **Selic target and decision history:** Time Series Management System (SGS), series 432 — the COPOM Selic target.
-   **CDI:** SGS series 4389 (annualized DI rate).
-   **IPCA accumulated over 12 months:** SGS series 433.
-   **Meeting calendar:** official COPOM schedule published by the Central Bank.
-   **Market expectations:** Focus Bulletin of the Central Bank — a weekly survey of more than 130 financial institutions; we use the median projection for the Selic at the next meeting. This is not the site's opinion: it is the market consensus measured by the Central Bank.
### When the page updates

On normal days, once a day. On **COPOM decision days** (always a Wednesday), the server polls the Central Bank periodically late in the afternoon and, as soon as the new rate is published, updates this page and **sends a notification to all users** informing them whether the Selic was hiked, cut, or held.

It stays at that level until the next meeting.

The **next Copom meeting** begins on Nov 3, 2026, with the decision announced on Nov 4, 2026 (44 days away). Market consensus from the central bank's Focus survey points to **a hold**, leaving the rate at 13.62% a year.

At 14.25%, it sits roughly triple the U.S. Fed Funds rate and offers one of the highest positive real yields on earth. ## What is the SELIC rate?

SELIC stands for **Sistema Especial de Liquidação e de Custódia** — the Special System for Settlement and Custody. It is Brazil’s system for clearing and settling transactions in federal government bonds. The “SELIC rate” (taxa SELIC) is the overnight interest rate at which banks lend to each other using those federal bonds as collateral.

In plain terms, it is Brazil’s equivalent of the U.S. Fed Funds rate or the ECB’s main refinancing rate — the floor from which all other interest rates in the economy are built. Consumer loans, corporate credit lines, savings account yields, and government bond returns all trace their pricing back to the SELIC.

There are technically two SELIC rates. The **SELIC Meta** (target rate) is the policy rate announced after COPOM meetings — currently 14.25% per year. The **SELIC Efetiva** (effective rate) is the actual average overnight rate, typically a few basis points below the meta. Fixed-income products and benchmarks use the efetiva in their calculations. When media and investors say “the SELIC rate,” they mean the meta.
## Who sets it: COPOM and Banco Central do Brasil

The SELIC rate Brazil relies on is set by **Banco Central do Brasil (BCB)** through its monetary policy committee, the **Comitê de Política Monetária (COPOM)**. Established in 1996, COPOM meets eight times per year — roughly every 45 days — over two days, with the rate decision announced on the Wednesday evening at market close.

The committee is composed of the BCB Governor and eight board members. Decisions are by majority vote. After each meeting, the BCB publishes a communiqué; the full minutes (the **Ata do COPOM**) follow roughly two weeks later and are closely parsed by analysts for forward guidance.
